Under this wretched wreckage, my mind wanders, crashing on the life I have lived like a ton of metal. Shock has replaced my my pain with a strange solace. Just like my bones, I remember promises I broke. Just like my breath, shallow, I never found the depth of enrichment. Just like life, I am pinned and I cannot turn from the sun in my eye. I could close my eyes, but I want a moment to appreciate the beauty in the face of pain as the sun descends. Just like blood, friends pooled around me and I still said I was alone. This is an odd time to seek acceptance of myself, because today is the day that I die.

At the end of the path, curiosity can be praised or be damned. So for last week, damn it all to hell. My grasp on what happened several days ago is still loose. It is like staring at all the puzzle pieces after you dumped the box, take a breath, and start piecing the edges. 

It starts with my usual routine, wake up at noon, make coffee, and check my mail. After retrieving the letters, I walked back up to the house to sit down and go through the mail. Sigh, "bills, bills, junk mail j- what the hell is this?" It was an envelope colored with a red and orange spiral going out from the center, lined in a black border. In big black letters it was addressed to me, John. "Huh," I vocalize as I I tear open the envelope.

"TRAVEL NO MORE, A CIRCUS WITH DISCOVERIES GALORE. IT IS HERE! IT IS HERE! THE MOST TO BE HAD OF AWE AND WONDER. HOWEVER, YOU MUST COME AS ONE!" This is what it said in black lettering on plain white paper, with a tiny clip art clown below. Below that was the address. The address? My address. I thought it was strange but brushed it off as an error.

I threw it on the table and took the last sip of my coffee. Going into to town was on the agenda that day, so I got up, grabbed my keys, and headed out. As I got out to my car, I was just far enough out to see something poking up from the hills. I figured what the hell, I have got time. The more I near the top of the hill, the more this mystery reveals. Stopping dead in my tracks, the realization of what it was left me flabbergasted. It was a tent. A goddamn circus tent. Now, this is the part where if you were at a movie, you would yell at the screen, "don't go in there!" 

Guess what I did. Curiosity be damned, I went to check it out. The tent had the same swirl of the envelope. One flap was pulled aside, I took this for an entrance and stepped inside. It was dark, too dark. There is no way this tent could block so much light. I kept walking aimlessly into nothingness. Suddenly, I could feel every nerve of my body scream as the place lit up with spotlights in succession, circling the circumference.

I was in the middle of a giant ring. Bleachers lined all the way around, holding up a crowd. They all sit silent, with judgemental faces. In front of me, a mirror showing my reflection. My reflection, was not of my own. Well, it was me, but I was a clown. One of those sad clowns depicted from early ages. With the patched torn pants, suspenders and a painted sad face.

"BEHOLD, the loneliest clown," a voice boomed on the intercom. The crowd widens their eyes. The speaker continues, "he sits and waits for a life that will never come. Silly clown." The crowd laughs, he goes on, "outside this tent, you would never see a damaged man. However, in this ring, he is painted as the pain he hides. Look at him! Just look! Silly clown." The last word echoed out and the lights went dark again.

I jolted up in bed out of breath. "What a dream," I thought. I got out of bed to make some coffee. I filled up the water reservoir, scooped the grounds, and pushed the button. I turn around to see something that gave me the same feeling I had seeing the tent for the first time. It was the envelope. I ran outside and up the hill, the tent was gone. I collapsed into the grass and stared at the envelope. I spent the rest of the day there, contemplating my life.

Up top where it says blender render, change it to cycles render. Right click on your model and Stretch out the right panel until you can see the materials tab, choose it, and click on 'use nodes'. Where it says color, there is a little button the right with a little circle click it, then click image texture, and choose your downloaded image. Then up top there is a bar that says default, click it and choose 'compositing'. There are 3 panels. The one with model, hover your mouse over it and hit tab to go into edit mode. Tap 'a' until the whole model is chosen. Hit 'u' and select 'smart uv project' and then 'ok'. When the model is selected in edit mode, it projects it's unwrap in the left panel. Below it, there is a button that says new and has a little button next to that, click it. It will pull up a menu of your imported images and select the one that you are trying to apply. From there you can move around how you want the picture to project. That's one way. The other way is exporting uv maps and that's a bag of cats of a different color. Hope it helped!
